question: Does the impact_load-threat_rank association change across cycle_code while threat_rank marginals remain stable?
input_root: configured TP2 regression input; path omitted
scope: Official labeled regression train only; the test target is unavailable and unused.

method.primary_periods: Sort unique train cycle_code values and split them into three equal-sized contiguous blocks; do not split individual cycles or inspect target to set boundaries.
method.sensitivity: Repeat the unique-cycle grouping using 2, 3, and 4 blocks; show row-pooled correlation and the equal-cycle mean of individual cycle correlations.
method.bootstrap: Resample observed cycles as clusters independently within first/last eleven-cycle blocks; fixed seed. This is exploratory sensitivity conditional on exchangeability, not a confidence interval or a serial-dependence-robust result.
method.nonlinearity: Exact-impact eta squared is in-sample variance decomposition, not predictive performance.
method.rank: Compare target to within-cycle average ranks of that same target. Report two-sided uniform KS distance as an effect size without a p-value, plus the separately labeled right-continuous ECDF gap. The implied mean 50+50/n is conditional on average-rank identity and does not prove source formula.

cycle_cluster_resampling.unit: cycle cluster; resampled within each observed endpoint 11-cycle block
cycle_cluster_resampling.exchangeability_assumption: Cycles are treated as exchangeable within each observed endpoint block.
cycle_cluster_resampling.interpretation: Exploratory cycle-cluster resampling sensitivity conditional on the observed 33 cycles. It treats cycles within each endpoint block as exchangeable, does not account for serial dependence, and is not a confidence interval or an inferential guarantee.

cycle_56_neighborhood_descriptive.interpretation: Local descriptive context only; cycle 56 is not treated as a prespecified break.

nonlinear_association_diagnostics.interpretation: In-sample grouped association only; no split, fit, or predictive performance claim.

interpretation_limits: Cycle correlations are descriptive summaries of one observed, ordered set of cycles; adjacent cycles and rows need not be independent.
Changing correlation is not by itself a structural break, causal mechanism, or statistically established drift.
Stable marginal ranks do not imply stable conditional association; percentile-like target construction may mechanically stabilize marginals.

Within-cycle rank identity examines target values against ranks of those same values. It does not establish target lineage, official semantics, or authorize target transformations for validation/test.

The near-50+50/n target mean follows mathematically if the observed rounded average-rank identity holds; it is a target-to-target construction implication, not independent evidence of how the official target was generated.
Uniform KS distances are descriptive effect sizes; no null-test p-value is used as evidence across the 33 observed cycles.
The right-continuous ECDF gap is one-sided and is distinct from the two-sided uniform KS distance.
Cycle code is treated as ordered numeric disclosure levels; calendar spacing and real-world time intervals are not inferred.
Cycle cluster resampling assumes exchangeability within endpoint blocks and does not account for serial dependence or future cycle uncertainty.
